html:
The Acjachemen are a Native American people of the coast of southern Orange County and northern San Diego County, California, around San Juan Capistrano. The Spanish called them Juaneños, after the mission.

They spoke a Uto-Aztecan language close to that of their Luiseño neighbours, and lived in villages by the creeks and coast, gathering acorns and seeds, fishing and hunting. In 1776 Junípero Serra founded Mission San Juan Capistrano on their land, and many Acjachemen were drawn into it. They built its great stone church, which an earthquake brought down in 1812, killing worshippers inside. Their northern neighbours were the Tongva. Today the Acjachemen are recognised by the state of California but not by the US government.
